propositions.text: The appellant, Tania Zulkoskey, appeals the Federal Court decision dismissing her judicial review application of the Commission's decision not to deal with her complaint as vexatious under CHRA paragraph 41(1)(d).

paragraphs.summary: The appellant appeals the Federal Court's dismissal of her judicial review of the Commission's vexatious complaint decision under CHRA paragraph 41(1)(d).

propositions.text: The appellant and spouse paid EI premiums; appellant gave birth to twins in 2009 and both requested 35 weeks EI parental benefits.
Spouse's request was approved; appellant's request denied because spouse already received maximum benefits under EI Act, which allows one set of benefits per pregnancy.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant and spouse requested EI parental benefits for twins; spouse's request approved, appellant's denied due to one set per pregnancy rule.

propositions.text: The appellant appealed the EI Commission's decision to the Board of Referees and Umpire; appeal stayed pending Martin case outcome.
Appellant initially proposed Martin outcome be binding but stay was granted without conditions.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant appealed EI denial; appeal stayed pending Martin case; appellant initially sought binding effect but stay was unconditional.

propositions.text: In Martin, this Court found EI Act provides 35 weeks parental benefits per pregnancy, not per child, and scheme is not discriminatory under Charter section 15(1).
Supreme Court denied leave to appeal Martin in 2013.

paragraphs.summary: Martin found EI benefits per pregnancy, not child, and no Charter discrimination; Supreme Court denied leave to appeal.

propositions.text: Appeals stayed pending Martin were transferred to SST-AD, which dismissed all appeals including appellant's, relying on Martin.
Appellant did not seek judicial review of SST-AD decision.

paragraphs.summary: SST-AD dismissed all appeals relying on Martin; appellant did not seek judicial review of SST-AD decision.

propositions.text: Appellant filed complaint with Commission alleging 'per pregnancy' restriction discriminated on family status ground.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant filed complaint alleging 'per pregnancy' restriction discriminated on family status.

propositions.text: Commission requested appellant's position on whether complaint should not be dealt with as vexatious under CHRA paragraph 41(1)(d).
Commission stated issue was whether complaint may have been dealt with through another process.

paragraphs.summary: Commission asked appellant if complaint should be dismissed as vexatious, considering if issues were dealt with elsewhere.

propositions.text: Section 40/41 Report prepared addressing vexatiousness and recommending Commission not deal with complaint as other process addressed discrimination allegations.
Parties responded to Report and to each other's submissions.

paragraphs.summary: Section 40/41 Report recommended not dealing with complaint as other process addressed discrimination; parties responded to Report and submissions.

propositions.text: Commission decided not to deal with complaint under paragraph 41(1)(d), adopting Section 40/41 Report's conclusion.
Commission accepted SST-AD relied on Martin and appellant's allegations were essentially same as Martin's under Charter section 15.

paragraphs.summary: Commission adopted Report and decided not to deal with complaint, accepting SST-AD relied on Martin and allegations were essentially same.

propositions.text: Appellant sought judicial review of Commission's decision as unreasonable and breaching procedural fairness.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant sought judicial review alleging Commission's decision was unreasonable and breached procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Application judge reviewed Commission's decision on reasonableness standard, affording high deference due to discretion and policy considerations.
Judge found Section 40/41 Report erred in concluding SST-AD finally determined discrimination allegations; appellant raised human rights only in CHRA complaint.
Judge concluded Commission's reliance on Martin alone justified decision not to deal with complaint as it negated prospect of success.

paragraphs.summary: Application judge found Commission entitled to high deference; Report erred on SST-AD's finality; reliance on Martin justified dismissal.

propositions.text: Judge applied correctness standard to procedural fairness, found appellant owed lesser degree of fairness under Baker factors.
Judge found Commission informed appellant and gave ample opportunity to submit; Report was neutral, thorough, and comprehensive.

paragraphs.summary: Judge found correctness standard for procedural fairness; appellant owed lesser fairness; Commission informed appellant and Report was thorough.

propositions.text: Issues: 1) Correct standard of review for Commission's decision? 2) Was decision reasonable? 3) Was decision procedurally fair?

paragraphs.summary: Court frames issues as standard of review, reasonableness, and procedural fairness of Commission's decision.

propositions.text: On judicial review appeal, Court must determine if application judge chose and applied correct standard of review, stepping into judge's shoes.

paragraphs.summary: Court must determine if application judge chose and applied correct standard of review, stepping into judge's shoes.

propositions.text: Parties agreed on reasonableness standard for reviewing Commission's decision; Court finds this appropriate.
Parties argued over margin of appreciation but Court finds only question is whether decision was reasonable under vexatious ground.
Reasonableness standard focuses on whether decision was reasonable given context, citing Wilson case.

paragraphs.summary: Parties agreed on reasonableness standard; Court focuses on whether decision was reasonable under vexatious ground, citing Wilson.

propositions.text: Section 40/41 Report is part of Commission's reasons; Commission's decision is verbatim copy of Report's conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: Section 40/41 Report forms part of Commission's reasons; decision copies Report's conclusion verbatim.

propositions.text: Commission informed appellant it considered complaint vexatious if issues may have been dealt with in another process under paragraph 41(1)(d).

paragraphs.summary: Commission considered complaint vexatious if issues may have been dealt with in another process under paragraph 41(1)(d).

propositions.text: In Figliola, SCC held similar provision allows dismissal if complaint substance dealt with in another proceeding, reflecting finality doctrines.
Figliola factors: concurrent jurisdiction, same legal issue, complainant's opportunity to meet case.
Figliola and Bergeron addressed cases where complainant had final decision on discrimination then raised it again in human rights proceeding.

paragraphs.summary: Figliola held similar provision allows dismissal if complaint dealt with elsewhere, reflecting finality doctrines; factors include jurisdiction, issue sameness, and opportunity.

propositions.text: Commission's approach to vexatiousness reflects Figliola factors: final decision, authority, issue sameness, all issues addressed, opportunity to raise issues, process differences.

paragraphs.summary: Commission's vexatiousness approach reflects Figliola factors including final decision, authority, issue sameness, and opportunity to raise issues.

propositions.text: Section 40/41 Report identifies appellant's other process as SST-AD EI Act appeal relying on Martin to dismiss appeal.
Commission reasons state SST-AD and this Court had jurisdiction to decide human rights issues.
Allegations in CHRA complaint are essentially same as those decided by SST-AD and this Court in Martin under Charter section 15.
Investigator acknowledges appellant did not raise CHRA before SST-AD but concludes Martin's Charter analysis sufficiently examined discrimination allegations similar to CHRA analysis.

paragraphs.summary: Report finds SST-AD appeal relied on Martin; both had jurisdiction; allegations same as Martin; Martin's Charter analysis suffices for CHRA claims.

propositions.text: The Commission unreasonably applied paragraph 41(1)(d) to the appellant's complaint.
The appellant did not raise human rights issues before filing her CHRA complaint; SST-AD's decision was limited to EI Act interpretation.
SST-AD applied Martin to find appellant entitled to one set of benefits per pregnancy, not per child, under EI Act.
Appellant did not raise discrimination allegations under Charter or CHRA for SST-AD to apply Martin.
Appellant did not receive a final decision on human rights issues at SST-AD.
Vexatiousness and Figliola factors do not apply to appellant's CHRA complaint as no final decision was received.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Commission unreasonably applied paragraph 41(1)(d); respondent concedes no prior human rights issues raised; SST-AD limited to EI Act; appellant did not raise discrimination; no final decision on human rights; vexatiousness factors do not apply.

propositions.text: Commission could reasonably dismiss appellant's complaint based on Martin alone if complaint has no reasonable prospect of success.
Complaint with no reasonable prospect of success is frivolous under paragraph 41(1)(d) (Love v. Canada).
Commission limited its analysis to vexatiousness and appellant's process, not frivolousness or discrimination allegations.
Commission asked parties to provide submissions on vexatiousness only, excluding evidence on discrimination allegations.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues dismissal based on Martin if complaint lacks success prospect; court notes Commission limited analysis to vexatiousness and excluded discrimination evidence.

propositions.text: Vexatious ground in paragraph 41(1)(d) is interpreted flexibly to prevent multiple proceedings and resource waste (Figliola).
Court adjudicated Martin's discrimination allegations under Charter; allegations may be essentially same as appellant's CHRA complaint.
Appellant's complaint may inevitably fail based on similarity to Martin's allegations.
Commission based decision solely on vexatiousness requiring final decision on discrimination allegations, which appellant lacks.
Martin's adjudication cannot substitute for appellant's final decision; Commission's decision is not defensible under vexatious ground.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains vexatious ground prevents re-litigation; Martin's adjudication not substitute for appellant's final decision; Commission's decision not defensible.

propositions.text: Commission misconceived SST-AD's dismissal basis, leading to focus on vexatiousness of appellant's CHRA complaint.
If Commission understood SST-AD's basis and Martin's conclusiveness, it could have raised frivolousness with appellant and heard submissions.
Commission can reconsider complaint's frivolousness and decide not to proceed if no prospect of success.
Court does not believe appellant's complaint is frivolous in colloquial sense and recognizes its importance to appellant and others.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Commission misunderstood SST-AD dismissal basis; Commission may reconsider frivolousness; court does not find complaint frivolous colloquially.

propositions.text: No need to decide if Commission breached procedural fairness; appellant's submissions on this are without merit.
Commission did not make clear, unambiguous promise to consider appellant's original position letter in decision.
Initial correspondence stated Commission would use parties' submissions to the report.
Correspondence seeking submissions stated Commission would decide based on report, complaint form, and submissions received.
Commission clearly communicated it would consider submissions made in response to Section 40/41 Report and followed this procedure.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no procedural fairness breach; Commission did not promise to consider original letter; correspondence stated decision based on submissions to report; Commission followed procedure.

propositions.text: Appellant had full opportunity to present position on why Commission should deal with complaint.
Arguments in original position letter repeated in Section 40/41 Report, including SST-AD's limited scope, Martin's inapplicability, and dismissal burden.
Commission reviewed appellant's submissions to the Report and response to respondent's submissions.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes appellant had full opportunity to present position; original arguments repeated in report; Commission reviewed all submissions.

propositions.text: Appeal allowed with costs; matter referred back to Commission for reconsideration.

paragraphs.summary: Court allows appeal with costs and refers matter back to Commission for reconsideration.
